articles.title: Cunha strikes late to deny Fulham and salvage point for Manchester United
articles.summary: To paraphrase a former Manchester United manager, Michael Carrick knew that the storm would come. Everything went a little too perfectly for him in the second half of last season. There would be ill winds at some point. Which was what Carrick could feel before this visit to Fulham.
body: Relief was surely the main thing. Because after the derby defeat by Manchester City last Sunday and the midweek Carabao Cup exit against Brighton – both at Old Trafford – Carrick was starring at an unwanted hat-trick. All this on the back of other wobbles since the opening weekend when United lost at Hull.

It was a darkly comic own goal by Lisandro Martínez that raised Fulham’s hopes of a first Premier League win under Alvaro Arbeloa. United have almost always won in this corner of south-west London in recent seasons. A crash against the team that started at the foot of the table was unthinkable.

Carrick and his team averted disaster when they caught a huge break with time almost up. There was little on for Matheus Cunha on the edge of the area, to the left of centre, and so he took on the shot for the near corner. The Fulham goalkeeper, Bernd Leno, looked to have it covered. Cue an almighty deflection off David Affengruber to send the ball spinning into the opposite corner.

articles.title: Maresca dismisses title talk as ‘too early’ after Manchester City take over at the top
articles.summary: ‘I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but expected a difficult game’ Semenyo scored twice in 5-3 victory against Sunderland. Enzo Maresca dismissed Manchester City pulling ahead in the title race after Sunday’s 5-3 win over Sunderland, with the manager stating it is “too early” in the season.
body: The frantic victory at the Etihad Stadium gave City 15 points from their opening five league matches, three more than Arsenal after the champions lost at Brighton on Saturday. Maresca was asked about his team being top before the three-week international break.

“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less. No doubt. But at the same time, we know that it’s quite early. The international break is good. We can review what we have done and what we can do better, and at the same time, we can relax a little more.”

Of the victory against Sunderland, Maresca said: “I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game – I knew how good they are, off the ball, very aggressive. I knew it was a difficult game but happy because we found a way to win the game.

“We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals. So that means that we create enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

articles.title: GB's Backstedt wins world time-trial silver
articles.summary: Britain's Zoe Backstedt, 21, wins silver in the women's time trial behind Switzerland's Marlen Reusser at the UCI World Road Championships in Montreal.
body: The 21-year-old Welsh rider could have opted to defend the under-23 title she won last year.

But instead she stepped up to elite level and finished 40.11 seconds behind defending champion Marlen Reusser of Switzerland, who retained her crown on her 35th birthday with a winning time of 50 minutes 24.44 seconds.
Backstedt, who started third from last, set the time to beat as she came home 5.43 secs quicker than Germany's Franziska Koch, who eventually finished third.
She told reporters that she started to dream of winning after making a storming start: "In the first half, when I heard the first time check, I was thinking 'OK, maybe it's possible'.

articles.title: Marlen Reusser holds off Zoe Backstedt to retain world time-trial cycling title
articles.summary: Swiss rider denies British challenger in Montreal. Franziska Koch finishes third, Demi Vollering eighth. Marlen Reusser retained her world time-trial title in Montreal on Sunday as her expected main challenger, Demi Vollering, finished a disappointing eighth.
body: Time-trial queen Reusser secured an ultimately comfortable victory, winning her second world championship after triumphing last year in Kigali – but not before young British rider Zoe Backstedt gave her a scare.

Backstedt had been quickest at the first two intermediate time-checks on the 39.2km (24.4 mile) course but Reusser powered away in the second half of the race to beat the 21-year-old by 40 seconds. Germany’s Franziska Koch finished third, a further six seconds back.
”It’s a good present,” said Reusser, who was competing on her 35th birthday. I also thought, win or not, I have something to celebrate.”

“From the side of pacing and understanding how fast you should go and how you should also cope with these challenges on the way, I was really nervous,” Reusser added. “I was not really sure, because we don’t have time trials like this often … I’m used to doing 20km.”

articles.title: McCullum hails Brook’s captaincy as England move top of T20 world rankings
articles.summary: Brook has ‘grown as captain and as a person’ – McCullum. England begin ODI series against Sri Lanka this week. England’s white-ball coach, Brendon McCullum, was full of praise for the captain, Harry Brook, after Saturday’s eight-wicket victory over Sri Lanka completed a T20 series whitewash and…
body: Brook, player of the T20 series against Sri Lanka, has now won 23 of his 26 completed games as captain. If he is not yet considered a suitable candidate as Test leader, the cap fits nicely in the smash ’n’ grab format.

“He’s grown not just as captain, but as a person as well,” said McCullum. “He seems very comfortable now as a leader of this side and the guys follow him, they trust him. Obviously his batting’s been on a different planet when it comes to T20 cricket, but I think his ability to do things differently based on what’s required with the conditions, and also against the opposition, has been probably the most impressive element.”

“Twenty20 is such an inconsistent game, so you can never take your eye off what you’re trying to achieve, but over the last 18 months or so we’ve found a nice level of consistency. We are not the finished article as yet, but the work we’ve done on the environment and the setup, and the depth that we’ve got in our side now is certainly encouraging.”
Alongside his relationship with Brook, there is a new guy in town to manage – McCullum’s old buddy and the new Test coach, Stephen Fleming, who was also at Old Trafford on Saturday.

articles.title: 'It might be time to wrap it up' - O'Neill ponders Celtic future after defeat
articles.summary: Martin O'Neill says he will use the international break to reflect on his position after Celtic suffer three consecutive defeats in big games.
body: He delivered a double few thought possible last season when the Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup were salvaged from the potential wreckage of one of Celtic's most tumultuous seasons.
He very nearly lifted the Uefa Cup in 2003 against a Jose Mourinho-inspired Porto who, the following season, won the Champions League.
His status as one of the club's all-time great managers is surely secure.
Which is perhaps why, so soon after returning to the club as its unlikely saviour, manager Martin O'Neill wondered out loud whether now, at the age of 74, it's finally time "to wrap it up".

articles.title: USA loss a game Ireland 'should have won' - Bemand
articles.summary: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".
body: USA, led by County Dublin-born head coach Jack Hanratty, fought back from trailing 31-12 at one stage of the second half to score four successive tries and claim a 40-36 comeback win.
A loss of discipline in the second half contributed to Ireland's loss after their impressive first-half display, and Bemand was frustrated that they let the game slip out of their control.

"We came out of the blocks, moved the ball well and got momentum and showed our style of play. USA then got some momentum using their power game and we've got to be a bit cuter and smarter in stopping teams getting that momentum," he told TG4.

"When teams get momentum the penalty count is more likely go up. There's bits we can control, not from a discipline perspective but in terms of our technical process, how we can be faster finishing tackles and getting break down pressure."

articles.title: Three straight losses, Martin’s got a lot of work to do
articles.summary: Earlier today Celtic suffered our third successive loss in eight days, and the second to our bitter rivals after losing 1-0 at Celtic Park, in yet another questionable performance by the players…Mar...
body: The crowd were up for it, and the players responded as they started impressively in a much changed 3-5-1-1 formation, looking more competent than our previous two fixtures (not that it would be difficult).

But it didn’t last as yet again we dwindled as the game progressed and suffered a sucker punch just after the half hour mark when we went a goal behind just a minute after a Kieran Tierney effort struck the bar.
We didn’t recover, and despite having a few half chances, in all truthfulness, we didn’t look like beaching the visitor’s defence today.

In these games you need your fair share of luck, and nothing went in our favour the entire afternoon. Ibrox centre back Fernandez already on a caution should have received his marching orders early on after obstructing Benjamin Nygren in a dangerous area, but referee John Beaton somehow waved play on, despite replays showing that it was a clear foul and a bookable offence.

articles.title: Cunha's late deflected equaliser grabs Man Utd point at Fulham
articles.summary: Matheus Cunha's deflected 89th-minute strike grabbed Manchester United a 1-1 draw at Fulham to take the edge off what appeared to be turning into a full-blown crisis for Michael Carrick's side going into the international break.
body: A horror-show own goal from Lisandro Martinez with 23 minutes to play, piled the pressure on United to snatch something from this match, following the midweek Carabao Cup collapse at home to Brighton and Manchester derby defeat last weekend.

A wicked flick off David Affengruber got them out of jail. But United are still in the bottom half of the Premier League after five games, 10 points adrift of table-topping neighbours City and looking miles off the level required to challenge the country's best sides this season. This is their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign.
Manchester United have won just five points from five league games this season – their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign (also 5 in 2014-15).

"A real mess" was how Sky Sports' Gary Neville described the own goal. Cunha was levered off the ball by Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey, whose stinging shot was parried by Senne Lammens. The 'keeper then saw Martinez stick out a boot and divert the ball back past him. Lammens' clumsy attempt to cut it out summed up United's chaotic defending.

articles.title: Palace secure valuable point at unbeaten Leeds
articles.summary: Crystal Palace secured a useful point at in-form and unbeaten Leeds as Pierre Sage's side produced a much-improved defensive display to hold the hosts to a goalless draw at Elland Road.
body: The stalemate was enough to lift Sage's side one point clear of the relegation zone heading into the three-week international break.

Palace arrived having conceded 11 goals in their opening four Premier League games but, after a cagey first half, grew into the contest and were the more threatening side after the break. Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net only for it to be ruled out for offside.

Leeds, unbeaten coming into the game after an impressive 4-1 win over Newcastle, struggled to reproduce that attacking fluency. Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who had scored in each of his previous five Premier League home games, was largely starved of service, eventually being denied by Walter Benitez after the break.

Palace had chances to snatch it late on, with Adam Wharton continuing to influence proceedings and Eddie Nketiah and Ismaila Sarr combining for an opening that Tarik Muharemovic brilliantly recovered to stop. Leeds threw on attacking reinforcements and switched shape, but could not find the breakthrough.

articles.title: Spaun wins BMW PGA Championship, McIlroy falters despite late surge
articles.summary: JJ Spaun outlasted a packed leaderboard of players on Sunday at the BMW PGA Championship, as the American capitalised on a stumble from Spain's Manuel Elvira to win his debut title at Wentworth.
body: An utterly thrilling final round of golf unfolded at Wentworth, with multiple players, including Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai and Elvira, racing to the finish line, but all struggled to pull away from the pack.
There was heartbreak for Elvira, who had the chance to leapfrog Spaun at the top of the leaderboard after tying the 2025 US Open champion with an eagle on the 17th hole.

With Spaun already in the clubhouse at 17 under, the Spaniard, who is ranked 294th in the Official World Golf Rankings, needed a birdie on the 18th to win his first-ever DP World Tour title, but he stumbled, finding a fairway bunker with his tee shot before sending his bunker shot well past the green.
He attempted to chip back on but agonisingly sent his shot into the bunker before ultimately confirming Spaun's two-stroke win with a double bogey.
